original_contribution: Opt-in SQLite leased delivery integrated with Huey execution, fenced ownership, atomic outcome acknowledgement/retry/callback handoffs and scheduler promotion. Original explicit feature contract, independent behavioral verifier, and reference implementation.

sources.finding: Current docs explicitly do not guarantee acknowledgements or at-least-once delivery.
Current SQLite dequeue deletes before execution; inspected base transaction and schedule APIs.
Public interruption-handler re-enqueue recipe is adjacent prior art; it does not handle SIGKILL, ownership generations or atomic retries.
Historical restart recovery request; no durable lease implementation in inspected upstream.

Public schedule enqueue failure issue; baseline includes latest per-enqueue exception-handling response. This task adds a broader original atomic recovery feature rather than reverting to an old vulnerable release.
Exclude already-shipped retries/backoff, chord improvements, graceful-signal and shutdown timeout work.

public_solution_overlap.known: Prior signal-handler recipe and schedule-transfer issue described above; no exact new API implementation found in current upstream source/issues checked.
public_solution_overlap.limit: Bounded repository/source/issue search, not exhaustive global fork search.

horizon.rationale: Requires coordinating persistent ownership, existing executor terminal paths, retries, callbacks, scheduler handoffs, schema compatibility, process lifetime and deterministic concurrency checks.

validation.local_oracle: 193 passed, zero skipped, zero errors (29 behavioral cases plus164 selected upstream cases). Reference-added public tests additionally2passed.
validation.untouched_baseline: New feature absent; ImportError for LeasedSqliteHuey produces verifier failure.

limitations: At-least-once delivery; no exactly-once external task/hook effects.
No automatic heartbeat; applications must renew long-running leases.
Requires leased consumers for the whole queue; ordinary destructive consumers are not supported on it.
No new exactly-once chord protocol, generic distributed storage protocol, or stronger-than-SQLite power-loss guarantee.
